'''Charles Niven''' (1845–1923) was a Scottish [[mathematician]] and physicist who spent most of his career at the [[University of Aberdeen]].  He published on mechanics, electricity, and heat.<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=migBAAAAYAAJ&dq=%22niven%22+cork+mathematics+born&pg=PA42 Niven, Charles] Some Account of the Last Bajans of King's and Marischal Colleges, p.42</ref>

== Life and work ==
Charles Niven studied mathematics at Aberdeen and was awarded a BA in 1863, and then studied at [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]]. Charles and his older brother [[William Davidson Niven|William D.]] were tutored by [[Edward Routh]] for the [[Mathematical Tripos]]. Charles became [[senior wrangler]] in 1867.{{sfn | Warwick | 2003 | p=154 }}

In 1867, Niven was appointed Professor of Mathematics at [[Queen's College Cork]], in Ireland{{sfn | Macdonald | 1923 | p=xxvii }} a position that [[George Boole]] had previously occupied.

From 1880, Niven was professor of Natural Philosophy in the [[University of Aberdeen]], and he was responsible for establishing the Physics Department in [[Marischal College]] in 1906.<ref>{{smallcaps|O'Connor & Robertson}}, MacTutor History of Mathematics.</ref> He retired at the end of 1922.{{sfn | Macdonald | 1923 | p=xxviii }}

Charles Niven was a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] from 1880 and honorary member of the [[Edinburgh Mathematical Society]] from 1883.<ref>[http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Obits2/Niven_Charles_RS_obituary.html Royal Society Obituary of Charles Niven]</ref>
